newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Balanced budget amendment gains Democrat vote.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Balanced budget amendment gains Democrat vote.

text.p: Democratic Sen. Max Cleland of Georgia said Friday he will vote for the Republican version of a constitutional amendment to require a balanced federal budget, bring the amendment within 4 votes of assured passage.

So far, 8 Democrats and all 55 Republicans have pledged to vote for the amendment but 67 are needed to pass a proposed amendment to the U.S. Constitution. An extremely close vote is expected in late February.
Cleland said he would favor a change that would protect Social Security, but if that is not approved, he would vote for the Republican plan.

Republican backers have said they believe 69 senators will vote for passage of the constitutional amendment. Their prediction counts those who have voted for it in the past and those who pledged to support some form of a balanced budget constitutional amendment during their 1996 campaigns.

"I have come to the conclusion that no viable alternative to constitutionally mandate a balanced budget exists now or in the immediate future," Cleland said in a statement. "I will vote in favor of S.J. Res. 1 (the Republican plan) regardless of the outcome of votes on the amendments I favor," he added.
